problem: Long-horizon and multi-goal navigation benchmarks (MultiON, GOAT-Bench, LHPR-VLN) are acoustically silent, while audio-visual navigation benchmarks tie sound to a single objective, so nothing tests goal-state-aware use of sound across a multi-goal mission.
motivation: Spatial audio gives non-line-of-sight cues to unexplored regions, but in a multi-goal mission a sound is only progress-dependent information. It does not identify which goal, category or instance it belongs to, and it can become a distractor once the subtask changes. The paper argues the core challenge is task-conditioned cue grounding, not generic multimodal fusion.
key_idea: Introduce LH-AVLN, a multi-goal (2-4) audio-visual-language navigation benchmark with heterogeneous goals (category, description, image) and alternating goal-associated sounds, plus PAG-Nav, a training-free agent that uses sound only for search and reserves submission for visual-semantic verification.
insight: Existing vision-language, memory-based and audio-visual agents nearly all fail full missions (SR <= 2.1-3.1), yet OSR is much higher (e.g. 66.5 for PAG-Nav ordered vs SR 2.3). The bottleneck is therefore converting goal-region visits into correct submit and verification decisions and mission-state management, not reaching the region. In the appendix ablation, removing audio from MAV-Nav drops unordered ISR from 35.2 to 17.2 and SoftSPL from 26.9 to 9.0, so audio helps search. There is no ablation of PAG-Nav's own components.
method: Benchmark task: a global mission of N in {2,3,4} goals, each given as category, description or reference image, with ordered and unordered variants. The agent gets RGB-D, pose and binaural audio, and acts with MoveForward/TurnLeft/TurnRight/Submit/Stop (at most N-1 Submits plus a final Stop).

Acoustic design: each target has a spatialized sound source, unfinished targets emit alternately, and a target's source is deactivated once it is completed. Audio does not reveal category, modality or goal index.

Benchmark construction: valid instances are checked with an open-vocabulary detector and navigable viewpoints, and cues (category, description, image) are built from them. Episodes require at least two goal modalities, unique target categories, geodesic separation and reachability. Splits are at scene level on Matterport3D in SoundSpaces 2.0.
Goal-conditioned perception (PAG-Nav): modality-specific encoders embed each goal, and the observation is projected into room, object and acoustic cues.

Temporal uniform semantic map: a shared-frame memory (R, O, A) of room semantics, persistent object hypotheses with goal associations, and audio memory. Audio memory has a max-intensity part and a bearing part.

Progressive goal-state planning: Search (frontier scoring by room prior, object prior and audio bearing), then Ground (candidate score from visual compatibility, context prior and audio intensity), then Verify (Submit only if verification passes and distance and heading thresholds are met).

MAV-Nav (appendix): a learned policy on a SAVN-CE scene-memory backbone with frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 goal encoders and a CNN audio encoder. It adds a goal selector for routing to pending goals and is trained with a Decoupled Target-Routing curriculum (DAgger warm start, PPO on two-goal tasks, then full PPO).

setting.backbone: PAG-Nav: modular training-free pipeline (detectors/encoders plus SG-Nav-style commonsense priors, exact models unspecified); MAV-Nav: SAVN-CE-style scene-memory Transformer with frozen CLIP ViT-B/32, trained with DAgger and PPO
setting.training_data: PAG-Nav: none (training-free). MAV-Nav: trained on LH-AVLN training scenes via DAgger warm start and PPO curriculum (scale not given).
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose + binaural audio, plus global mission text/image/category goals
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Submit, Stop
setting.privileged: none for the agent (GT target identity and location are used only for episode generation and evaluation)

results: All baselines get near-zero full-task SR (0.0-2.1 ordered/unordered), e.g. MTU3D 1.7/2.1 and 3D-Mem 0.0/1.0. PAG-Nav is best in both settings, with SR 2.3/3.1, ISR 17.5/31.5 and OSR 66.5/55.6, but full-mission success stays very low. The appendix MAV-Nav reaches unordered SR 6.0 and ISR 35.2 on 550 episodes, though it is not compared in the main table.
limitations: Absolute full-mission success stays under 7% for every method, so the benchmark is mostly diagnostic. The paper offers no analysis of why, and it has no ablations of PAG-Nav components and lists incomplete baseline rows (SCOPE, AVLen, DAgger-only, Direct PPO).

The main-table evaluation set, the number of benchmark scenes and episodes, and the split protocol are underspecified. PAG-Nav's perception models and hyperparameters are not described, and it is evaluated only in simulation.
MAV-Nav numbers are on a different setting and are not directly compared with PAG-Nav, and the interpretation of ordered vs unordered results is speculative.
